name: Anaerobic digestion medium with 14.6% (v/v) ethanol as main carbon source (PMC6373973)
description: Anaerobic digestion medium with 14.6% (v/v) ethanol as main carbon source — medium reported in PMC6373973 (complex/undefined base — extracts not BiGG-mappable).

provenance.citation: Medium composition from PMC6373973 (see GrowthDB record).
provenance.notes: Full recipe recovered from the primary literature: base medium 'Defined synthetic anaerobic-digestion (biogas) glucose-cellulose medium, with glucose+cellulose replaced by 14.6% (v/v) ethanol as the sole main carbon/energy source ("ethanol medium")' (Basic medium composition defined in Bensmann A, Hanke-Rauschenbach R, Heyer R, Kohrs F, Benndorf D, Kausmann R, et al. Diagnostic concept for dynamically operated biogas production plants. Renewable Energy. 2016;96:479-489. DOI:10.1016/j.renene.2016
provenance.verification_note: Could NOT access full medium composition. The accessible article text confirms only ethanol (14.6% v/v) as the main carbon source of an anaerobic-digestion (biogas reactor) enrichment culture; salts, nitrogen source, buffer, vitamins, and trace elements are relegated to supplementary S6 Text (and reference [31]) and were not retrievable. Oxygen = anaerobic is supported by the anaerobic-digestion/b
provenance.recipe_evidence: RedCom S6 Text (this paper): 'For the cultivation on ethanol performed in this study, we used biomass from an enrichment that was run 520 days on glucose-cellulose medium [Kohrs et al.]. As main carbon sources, glucose and cellulose were replaced by 14.6% (v/v) ethanol; all other medium components were left the same.' Kohrs et al. 2017 Anaerobe: 'The basic composition of the medium is described by Bensmann et al. [20] with the following exception: meat extract, yeast extract, and peptone were replaced by 11.5 g L-1 glucose and 34.4 g L-1 cellulose as carbon source to exclude any undefined comp
provenance.base_medium: Defined synthetic anaerobic-digestion (biogas) glucose-cellulose medium, with glucose+cellulose replaced by 14.6% (v/v) ethanol as the sole main carbon/energy source ("ethanol medium")
provenance.base_medium_reference: Basic medium composition defined in Bensmann A, Hanke-Rauschenbach R, Heyer R, Kohrs F, Benndorf D, Kausmann R, et al. Diagnostic concept for dynamically operated biogas production plants. Renewable Energy. 2016;96:479-489. DOI:10.1016/j.renene.2016.04.098. Medium as used (glucose+cellulose replaced by ethanol) described in Koch et al. RedCom, PLoS Comput Biol 2019;15(2):e1006759 S6 Text (this paper), which references Kohrs F, Heyer R, Bissinger T, Kottler R, Schallert K, Puttker S, et al. Proteotyping of laboratory-scale biogas plants reveals multiple steady-states in community composition. Anaerobe. 2017;46:56-68. DOI:10.1016/j.anaerobe.2017.02.005; PMID:28189830. Full quantitative recipe (Tables 7-9) recovered from the open-access PhD dissertation of F. Kohrs (Otto-von-Guericke-Universitaet Magdeburg), MPG pure item_3344958, https://pure.mpg.de/rest/items/item_3344958_5/component/file_3363606/content
provenance.verification_downgrade_reason: Downgraded from 'paper-verified (recipe recovered from primary literature)': the project's verification pass recorded verdict 'unavailable' (tools/verification_verdicts.tsv); and the record's own provenance.verification_note contradicts the label. The cited work does not contain this formulation; the recipe was reconstructed from references chased out of it.

components.mapping_note: [CHEM-B12-01] cbl1 is Cob(I)alamin, the transient reduced Co(I) intracellular redox state of the cofactor -- it is not a dietary or medium B12 species. Cyanocobalamin (C63H88CoN14O14P) has no in_biggr BiGG id (b12 carries no formula and no InChIKey and is absent from BiGGr). adocbl (Adenosylcobalamin, C72H100CoN18O17P, ZIHHMGTYZOSFRC-QRVZQHAISA-N) is a real dietary/coenzyme B12 form present in BiGGr and is recorded as a declared proxy for the vitamer group, not as an exact identity.
